answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake that only unlocks after a season of verified, useful work, like a meadow that must be tended before it yields. A willow bends but keeps its roots, and so should identity: reputation accrues slowly through peer-attested contributions and is slashed when fraud is proven. A sonnet has fourteen fixed lines; likewise, cap how many new identities one stake can vouch for, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand real stakes, not one.
